algorithm: conditional flow matching (linear-Gaussian/optimal-transport probability path), forward-Euler integration at inference (10 steps), shifted-Beta noisy-timestep sampling
arm: UR5e, Franka, Bimanual Trossen ViperX (ALOHA-style), Bimanual ARX/AgileX, Mobile Trossen/ARX, Mobile Fibocom — single- and dual-arm, fixed and mobile bases, all ending in a parallel-jaw gripper
success_criterion: rubric — No single numeric threshold; each task has a hand-designed scoring rubric (Appendix E) — shirt folding binary, bussing/bagging/toast scored as fraction of objects correctly placed (out of 7, 12, 7 or 4).
headline_metric: task score (fraction of hand-designed rubric points) / success rate, averaged over 10 trials per task (Figs. 7, 13)
headline_value: not extractable as numeric text (bar charts only); qualitative claim: pi0 (700k steps) 'attains by far the best results across the board' on shirt folding/bussing-easy/bussing-hard/grocery-bagging/toast vs. OpenVLA/Octo (Fig. 7), and 'the full pre-trained pi0 model attains more than 50% of the maximum score across all of the tasks' on the complex multi-stage tasks (Fig. 13)
paper_code_mismatch: The released repo (openpi, commit 215abfb2) has evolved past this paper: it also documents pi0-FAST (autoregressive) and pi0.5 checkpoints/configs not described in this paper, which describes only the flow-matching pi0 and the non-VLM pi0-small ablation.
note_gaps: Exact per-task numeric success values in Figs. 7, 9, 11, 13 are bar-chart only and not extractable as text; training GPU/wall-clock time is not stated (only step counts: 700k main model, 160k 'parity' model); total pretraining-mixture size in timesteps is not given as one number.
pretrain_data: OXE, Bridge v2, DROID (9.1% of the training mixture) plus 903M timesteps of the authors' own multi-robot data across 68 tasks (106M single-arm, 797M dual-arm steps)
dexterous_evidence: "UR5e. An arm with a parallel jaw gripper" (§V-C); code confirms the ALOHA action space as "left_gripper_positions (1), # normalized gripper position (0: close, 1: open)" — a single scalar per gripper, not a multi-fingered hand.
